evidence: src/domain/entities/Project.ts: static create(id, name) { const trimmed = name.trim(); if (trimmed.length === 0) throw new ValidationError('Project name must not be empty'); return new Project(id, trimmed); }

src/domain/entities/User.ts: static create(id, name) { const trimmed = name.trim(); if (trimmed.length === 0) throw new ValidationError('User name must not be empty'); return new User(id, trimmed); }, which matches Project.create line for line
src/domain/entities/Task.ts: readonly title: TaskTitle; NewTaskProps.title: TaskTitle, so title validation is delegated to a value object rather than done inline
Project.name and User.name are typed as raw string, while Task uses the TaskTitle, DueDate and TaskStatus value objects
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three entities belong together: they are the domain entities of a task-management model. The problem is how they handle their invariants. Project.ts and User.ts each repeat the same non-empty trimmed-name rule inside their static create factories: trim the name, check the length is not 0, throw ValidationError, then build the object with the trimmed name. Task.ts handles the same kind of rule differently. Its title is the TaskTitle value object, so title validation lives in one reusable abstraction. Project and User instead take raw strings and validate them inline. So one rule is written in two places, and the value-object pattern used elsewhere in the module is not applied consistently. This is borderline, because project names and user names are different domain concepts and their rules could reasonably diverge. But as written, the rule is identical and repeated, which matches the rubric's fail condition about duplicating a rule.

violations.message: Project.create repeats the non-empty trimmed-name check that also appears in User.create, and validates a raw string name instead of using a value object like TaskTitle in Task.ts.
User.create repeats line for line the name-validation rule from Project.create (trim, check for empty, throw ValidationError) instead of putting it in one shared value object or helper.
